caught_incidents.confirmation_excerpt: Reject invalid integer constants in unevaluated preprocessor operands Clang was previously accepting invalid code like: ``` #if 1 ? 1 : 999999999999999999999 #endif ``` because the integer constant (which is too large to fit into any standard or extended integer type) was in an unevaluated branch of the conditional operator. Similar invalid code involving || or && was also accepted and is now rejected. Fixes #134658
caught_incidents.report_excerpt: Clang not diagnosing invalid literals in unevaluated contexts I cannot find anything that permits a compiler to accept the following (in either the C or C++ standards). Integer literals must have a type and a value in range for that type: #if 0? 999999999999999999999999999999999999: 3 #endif Clang accepts it even with -pedantic-errors. It seems that GCC, EDG and MSVC all reject it.
